In this issue

1.  AI Tool Improves Resident Confidence, Knowledge of Noninvasive Respira…

The one thing

AI Tool Improves Resident Confidence, Knowledge of Noninvasive Respiratory Support

Browser-based AI simulation could give every resident standardized practice with high-risk, low-frequency scenarios like escalating respiratory support. Educators should still look for objective skill outcomes before relying on it.

Pulmonology Advisor (report on a CHEST 2026 Annual Meeting abstract)

Read our summary →

AI vs physician

Comparative Cost of Care Recommended by Large Language Models versus Treating Physicians

This week’s result: physicians outperformed ai.

Trainees who use LLMs to draft plans should watch for over-ordering, because a plan can sound thorough and still add cost with no clear benefit. Educators can use this study to teach high-value care alongside AI literacy.

NEJM AI

Read our summary →

AI vs physician

AI-based clinician decision support system for diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases: a multicenter, randomized trial

This week’s result: AI helped improve.

This is one of the few randomised trials of AI used alongside specialists in real patients, and it shows the biggest gains in a rare-disease field where expertise is scarce. Trainees should note that it tested AI as an aid to specialists, not as a replacement, and that the evidence on management benefit is still exploratory.

AI MEDICINE COLLECTIVE

The Weekly Digest

OCTOBER 17 – OCTOBER 23, 2026   •   A TWO-MINUTE READ

In this issue

1.  Radiologists, LLMs fail at spotting AI-generated chest x-rays

2.  AI vs physician: physicians outperformed ai

3.  Tool of the week: HEART Score Calculator

 

The one thing

Radiologists, LLMs fail at spotting AI-generated chest x-rays

The models and the readers made different kinds of mistakes, so having one check the other does not reliably catch fake images. The authors suggest that tracking where an image came from at the point it is created, for example with watermarking, should be the main safeguard, with visual review as a backup.

AuntMinnie (reporting a study in the Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine)

Read our summary →

AI vs physician

Comparative Cost of Care Recommended by Large Language Models versus Treating Physicians

This week’s result: physicians outperformed ai.

Trainees who use LLMs to draft plans should watch for over-ordering, because a plan can sound thorough and still add cost with no clear benefit. Educators can use this study to teach high-value care alongside AI literacy.
